message:
fix(test): a shell launch happens later, so deleting the fixture afterwards is too late

The suite fired a launch through the shell, finished, and removed its
directory. Explorer got to the request afterwards and put "Windows cannot
find ...\ScnClient.exe" on the user's desktop. From a test, on a machine
somebody was using.

Checking the file exists before asking is not a defence and the comment
saying it was has been corrected. The check answers a question about the
past; the launch happens later, in another process, and the gap between
them is exactly where the deletion happened. What prevents the dialog is
the file still being there when the request lands -- a question about who
may delete it and when.

So the fixture is a real executable that records itself and exits, rather
than a copy of the command interpreter. Two things follow. The suite can
WAIT for evidence that a launch actually arrived instead of assuming a
timeout was long enough, and nothing is left running afterwards -- which
is what made a sweep necessary, and the sweep is what came to terminate
processes it could not identify.

The wait happens inside the scenario that fired the launch, because the
next one clears the witness; asking at teardown asks about a different
run, and the answer would be "it never happened". If it truly never
arrives the directory stays, with the reason printed. Litter inside the
repository is a small price against a dialog on somebody's screen.

The relaunch suite had the same shape -- fixtures in %TEMP%, a shell
launch, then remove the tree -- and gets the same treatment plus a root
inside the repository.

Nothing in %TEMP% was deleted, nothing was killed by name, and the dialog
was left for the user to close.
